**Take advantage of covered screenings and preventive care.** Type 2 diabetes typically


develops


gradually, so it is important to look for risk factors (family history, physical inactivity, obesity) and warning signs (excessive thirst


,


consistent fatigue). Eligible Medicare beneficiaries can receive up to two screenings within a 12-month period through Medicare Part B, and typically with no copay. Before your appointment, ask whether any


additional


services could result in a bill.


**Consider a Medicare plan focused on diabetes.** If you have diabetes, you may be eligible for a Medicare Advantage plan called a Chronic Condition Special Needs Plan (C-SNP). This type of Medicare Advantage plan often provides coordinated care for people with qualifying chronic conditions, access to lifestyle coaching programs, and savings on diabetes medications and supplies. Before choosing one, check whether your doctors


participate


, whether your prescriptions are covered and what you would pay for the care you use.


**[Recent eHealth research](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/news/survey-half-of-medicare-beneficiaries-have-skipped-medical-care-in-the-past-year-due-to-confusion-over-their-coverage)** shows that 78% of Medicare beneficiaries with diabetes enrolled in a C-SNP credit the plan with lowering their A1C levels.


**Use dental and vision benefits to avoid potential diabetes-related complications.** M

isn't


only about monitoring blood sugar. Diabetes can also contribute to complications affecting oral and eye health. Regular dental care can help


identify


and address gum disease, which is more common among people with diabetes and, if left untreated, can make the condition harder to control. Routine eye exams are important because they can help with early detection of diabetes and reduce the risk of developing vision problems caused by this chronic condition.
